key_risks.title: Weather parametric ≠ curtailment
key_risks.body: Swiss Re Corporate Solutions markets the first UK red-weather-warning parametric policy (Willis partnership) and four disclosed non-damage products (trigger gap 0/4). Weather-index triggers capture meteorological events, not NESO gate status or distribution curtailment orders — UK power/DC cedants hedged on Met Office warnings may still face basis risk on grid-firmness losses.

key_risks.title: Diversified book hides UK DC tail
key_risks.body: Broad multi-line book dilutes single-grid correlation (aggregation 1/4, book concentration 2/4). UK power and data-centre cedants are secondary to the renewable-energy and parametric weather franchise — correlated UK DC stress may be immaterial at group level but invisible in cedant-level monitoring until renewals.

key_risks.title: AA- parent, assessed cedant mix

key_risks.body: SCOR Syndicate disclosed energy/power GWP share of 0.15% (£0.538m of £356m) — book concentration 0/4. UK power and DC cedants are incidental to the global book; latent rating 2/4 suggests underwriting interest exceeds disclosed premium. Provisional tier: disclosed share may understate Lloyd's energy panel participation.

key_risks.title: Parametric thought, treaty gap
key_risks.body: Alternative Solutions team builds weather-index structures (trigger gap 1/4, product fit 3/4) including wind-index windfarm revenue cover, but standard energy treaties remain physical-damage led. UK cedants without parametric extensions face residual basis risk on non-damage curtailment relative to Munich Re or Nephila.

key_risks.title: A+ capital, negligible UK tail
key_risks.body: S&P A+ parent support (capital 3/4) and globally diversified book (aggregation 1/4) mean UK grid-constraint PML is immaterial to group solvency. Risk is opportunity cost — SCOR may underwrite UK DC cedants on legacy triggers without pricing the non-firm tail competitors are building parametric products for.

key_risks.title: European renewables UK correlation
key_risks.body: Hannover Re's energy and engineering segment scores aggregation/correlation 2/4 with explicit UK power correlation within a broader European portfolio. Offshore wind, solar, BESS and data-centre cedants under CMP434/435 connections reform create mixed firm/non-firm exposure (non-firm intensity 2/4). A significant UK grid-constraint event could produce correlated claims across multiple European cedants Hannover assumes.

key_risks.title: Parametric capability, treaty PD dominance
key_risks.body: Hannover's parametric solutions practice (trigger gap 1/4, product fit 3/4) can structure index-triggered reinsurance, but standard energy treaties remain physical-damage dominated. UK cedants on annual PD-led covers face partial basis risk when curtailment losses lack damage — parametric capability exists but is not the default ceded structure.

key_risks.title: Project-finance tenor mismatch
key_risks.body: Multi-year treaties and project-finance-linked energy structures (tenor mismatch 2/4) extend cover against near-zero UK non-firm curtailment loss history. AA- S&P rating and capital 4/4 provide headroom, but long-dated structured covers on BESS and DC campus build-outs carry model risk on thin comparable experience.

key_risks.title: Cat aggregation masks grid events
key_risks.body: RenaissanceRe's property-cat-led specialty book scores aggregation/correlation 2/4, but accumulation models target named nat-cat perils rather than man-made grid-infrastructure events. UK power-curtailment correlation is not a modelled scenario for the dominant cat franchise — several energy cedants could loss-hit concurrently without appearing in RDS-style energy accumulation.

key_risks.title: Parametric gap vs cat peers
key_risks.body: Trigger gap 2/4 with only two disclosed non-damage products; product fit 2/4. Specialty marine/energy includes renewables but availability-index structures lag Nephila or Swiss Re Corporate Solutions. UK cedants on physical-damage-led RenRe treaties face basis risk when curtailment losses lack insurable damage — legacy wording leaves more spillover than parametric competitors.

key_risks.title: Provisional UK energy slice
key_risks.body: 20% sub-factor weight disclosed; book concentration 1/4 and non-firm intensity 1/4 are assessed. RenRe's UK power/DC cedant share is not filing-quantified. A+ capital (4/4) comfortably covers the inferred minor energy tail, but underwriting action on emerging UK DC cedants relies on specialist judgment rather than register evidence.

key_risks.title: Offshore-heavy PD trigger gap
key_risks.body: Arch Re scores trigger gap 3/4 with a single disclosed non-damage product and product fit 1/4 — among the weakest parametric profiles in this batch. Energy cedants are upstream offshore and conventional power on firm connections; UK data-centre and renewable cedants with non-firm links are negligible today but inherit physical-damage treaty wordings that exclude pure availability losses.

key_risks.title: Nat-cat models, not grid PML
key_risks.body: Arch Analytics focuses on RMS/AIR nat-cat perils; energy pricing is experience-rated without documented curtailment telemetry. Aggregation/correlation 1/4 reflects geographic diversification, but accumulation targets hurricane and earthquake scenarios — a UK transmission constraint event would not appear in Arch's dominant property-cat PML framework.

key_risks.title: A+ capital vs sidelined prep
key_risks.body: AM Best A+ (disclosed) gives capital 4/4 — deep balance sheet relative to the minor UK power tail (book concentration 1/4). Margin-of-safety 22.5 reflects low preparedness (55/100) not capital strain. The risk is mispricing emerging UK DC cedants on legacy triggers, not solvency under a grid shock.

key_risks.title: DC-renewable correlation stack

A UK grid-constraint or regional low-wind event can hit multiple ceded structures in the same quarter — aggregation/correlation scores 3/4. Collateralised ILS capacity absorbs individual losses, but correlated weather–curtailment episodes are not separately capital-modelled.
